newsitem.title: USA: Fed to ensure stable prices-Richmond Fed Broaddus.
newsitem.headline: Fed to ensure stable prices-Richmond Fed Broaddus.

text.p: The Federal Reserve remains committed to its long-term goal of price stability, Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond President Alfred Broaddus said on Friday.

"Rest assured that we are firmly committed to continuing this progress toward price stability and then maintaining it once it is achieved," Broaddus told the Independent Banks of South Carolina at Hilton Head Islands, South Carolina.
"We at the Fed will work diligently to keep inflation low," Broaddus added.
The text of the speech was made available in New York.
The Richmond Fed president acknowledged that deregulation in the U.S. banking industry would result in more mergers and consolidation in that sector.
However, Broaddus expected community banking to remain an important part of the American economic landscape.

"Community banks will probably remain the most efficient providers of credit to at least one clearly identifiable and extremely important economic group, the small business borrower for whom standard creditworthiness information is difficult to obtain," Broaddus also said.
